messages:
deploy-bot: deploy finished: rollout "waveflip" -> canary 10% at 2026-03-17T12:45:45Z. Monitoring: p99 latency jump on runtime service (text-generate) from ~220ms -> ~1.8s. Paging oncall.

ashley: taking pager. oncall handover, i'm live in #incidents. pinging runtime + sRE. :phone:

incident-bot: INCIDENT CREATED: INC-20260317-4732 | severity: high | link: https://incidents.redwood.internal/INC-20260317-4732

mike: saw the alert, looking at kernels/selector. can someone paste recent node logs? i'm checking kernel fallback metrics.

lina: grabbing logs from canary instances now.

lina: logs snippet:
```
[2026-03-17T12:46:02Z] runtime: request_id=abcd1234 latency=1823ms model=mosaic-v1
[2026-03-17T12:46:03Z] kernel_selector: preferred='quant-opt' -> fallback='generic' (missing kernel: qint8_attn_v2)
[2026-03-17T12:46:03Z] batcher: window_ms=500 target_batch=8 current_batch=1
[2026-03-17T12:46:04Z] kv_cache: hit_rate=94% eviction=0
```

mike: kernel_selector fallback confirmed. that explains per-token CPU increase and p99 tail. also seeing microbatching collapse (batch size small -> overhead per request increases).

ashley: what's the mitigation? kill-switch flag for rollout?

lina: two options: 1) flip feature-flag waveflip.off to cut traffic to canary immediately, or 2) rollback the rollout to previous stable. flip is faster.

mike: agree flip first to stop spillover. while flipped, we can decide rollback vs recompile kernels.

ashley: lina, can you run the flag flip? deploy-bot is not gated for rollouts.

lina: running kill-switch now.

lina:
```
# internal feature flag API
curl -X POST "https://flags.redwood.internal/api/v1/flags/waveflip" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $OP_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"state":"off","reason":"canary latency spike - kernel fallback"}'
```

deploy-bot: feature flag waveflip set to OFF by lina at 2026-03-17T12:47:15Z. Traffic to canary scaled down to 0%.

ashley: monitoring dashboard... p99 dropping.

lina: p99 dropped from 1.8s -> 320ms within 60s after flip. nice.

mike: throughput still ~10% below baseline. digging into why batching not recovering — some warmup state in scheduler.

dan: support: receiving a handful of customer reports showing timeouts on /v1/generate around 12:46-12:58 UTC. I have a short list of impacted API keys, escalating to accounts.

ashley: product/ops: can we get impact estimate? dan, how many orgs? any enterprise customers?

dan: ~6 orgs, 2 enterprise customers with elevated latencies, ~0.8% of total requests during spike window returned 500/timeout. No major data loss.

sam: recommending we still roll back the canary to be safe (fully revert the waveflip change), and run a kernel recompile for quant path before re-release.

mike: +1 rollback. recompile may take hours depending on queue. rollback should be quick and allow normal batching to resume.

ashley: initiating rollback per runbook.

ashley:
```
# rollback command (internal deploy CLI)
redwood-deploy rollback --service runtime --release waveflip --to stable-20260315
```

deploy-bot: rollback triggered by ashley at 2026-03-17T12:51:10Z. Rolling traffic back to stable-20260315 across regions.

infra-bot: autoscaler ramping to stable weights; draining canary nodes.

lina: seeing additional improvement: p99 -> 260ms, throughput back to ~98% baseline after pools stabilize.

mike: filing ticket to add kernel-availability check to rollout gating: fail rollout if quant-optimized kernel not present. also add pre-rollout synthetic load test for microbatch behavior.

ashley: oncall -> lina handing off. Lina, you own the incident until postmortem done.

lina: got it. will draft postmortem and list action items: kernel gating, rollout precheck, rollout graduality adjustments, communications to impacted customers.

product-ops: preparing proactive customer comms for 2 enterprise customers. will send note in 30m.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: reduced to severity: medium (impact contained). root cause suspected: missing optimized quant kernel causing fallback to generic kernel + degraded batching behavior during canary traffic pattern. timeline and mitigation recorded.

ashley: thanks team. final ask: attach timeline + logs to INC-20260317-4732 and schedule 1hr postmortem review at 16:00 UTC.

lina: will upload attachments and schedule. incident RESOLVED at 2026-03-17T13:02:10Z (service stable). Postmortem in progress.

dan: support note queued to send to affected orgs (explain latency spike, window, no data loss).

mike: follow-ups: (1) gate rollout on kernel presence, (2) add microbatch smoke to canary traffic, (3) improve dashboard alerting to separate kernel-fallback vs other latency.

ashley: closing thread. :white_check_mark:
